answer: Each submission hangs on the copper of a task receipt, and the basalt is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, re-queued for a second panel, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Written in a cause and effect, two sentences register, it stays short. Reaching the sable of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
